title: MCP event-analysis contract
evidence_order: 2. first digital interlock and quench_unit / quench_units_with_quen_assert
3. per-cavity sequence (90/50/10% times), not a class-level median
4. reliability flags: tau_reliable, cavity_tau_span_us, per-cavity tau
5. image panel mapping: images[].scope and visible_channels
6. root cause stated in notes, then cause_candidates as hypotheses
rules: physics.class is an observational pattern, never a root-cause label.
If tau_reliable=false, do not quote a single decay tau; report the 90-10% span and two-stage/slow tail.
A cavity probe dip followed by a rise is beam-loading/phase-slip oscillation, not 'recovery'.
RDY_KSU# can be downstream of QUEN_CM#, ARC_CM#, VAC_CM#, or a beam-loss event; check the earliest digital.
Do not call multi-cavity collapse simultaneous unless the per-cavity 50/10% times agree.
Forward power around 1.1-1.2 is the post-limit value from over-input protection (~1.2x), not the LLRF demand.
Do not invent He-cooling loss, thermal runaway, or QL collapse unless the note or logs state it.
For a CM single-fault example, prefer CM ARC or CM flowmeter/water-flow events; quench events often mix in multi-cavity/propagation effects.
tool_sequence: postmortem_search_notes(query) only for similar operator wording, not for counts

good_examples.why: CM3 ARC only; single cavity collapse; first digital ARC_CM3; clean CM single-fault example.
KSU3 HVPS water flow low; CM3 station RF off; one cavity collapses; clean flowmeter/station example.

bad_examples.why: CM1 quench, but class=rf_trip and 3 cavities eventually collapse; tau_reliable=false. Do not use as the canonical single-CM example, do not quote tau=17 ms, and do not call the collapses simultaneous.
